en:
I'm to go first?
Very well.
Let me see... shall I introduce myself first?
My name is Akemi Iwashita.
I'm a third-year.
Now then, to get right to it, {a}...?
You're in Class 1-E, aren't you?
Then your classroom is on the third floor of the new school building.
At the far end of the long hallway.{p}...Isn't that right?
Yes
No
I don't know which staircase you use, but you always pass through the front entrance on the first floor, don't you?{p}Did you know there's a shabby old bulletin board there?
I know it
I don't know it

I see, you don't know it.
It isn't a very eye-catching thing, after all.
Even so, I'm sure you've seen it a few times.
You just haven't noticed it.
Or perhaps you've been avoiding it without realizing...?
The story I'm about to tell you is about that bulletin board.{p}

That bulletin board, you see, was left by students here... that is, by seniors many generations before us, as a graduation memento.
After all, its frame has the words
'The Graduating Class'
carved into it.
But as for when that was...
Unfortunately, no one knows for certain.
According to teachers who've been here a long time, the board was there even before the new school building was built.{p}

Back then, it stood in a corner of the schoolyard, they say.
When construction on the new school building began...
they decided to expand the schoolyard at the same time, so the board was moved as well.
So that the students could use it more easily...
But you know, not many people actually used that board.
And no wonder.{p}

...A terrible curse is sealed inside that bulletin board...
That was a famous rumor among the students.
'If you look at the board at midnight, a message from the spirit world will be posted on it, and whoever reads that message will die within three days.'
'Anyone who tears a notice off the board without permission will be cursed.'
'Anyone whose roll number and name are posted on the board on Friday the 13th will meet with misfortune.
It is the work of the ghost of a student who killed themselves some time ago.'
'If you use a brand-new thumbtack on the board, you will be injured without fail.'
...I've heard all sorts of rumors.
But you know, it's a fact that eerie notices have been posted there, and that students who used the board have had accidents.
They say some were caught up in crimes and lost their lives, and some even killed themselves.{p}
Say, {a}.{p}Do you know what that bulletin board is called?
I know
I don't know

Heh heh heh...
I'll tell you.
It's called 'the Board of Death.'
A loathsome name, isn't it?{p}

Mind you, only the students called it that...
To the teachers, the board's curse was nothing but a story children had made up.
"There's no such thing as ghosts!"
Some teachers insisted on just that and nothing else, so there was no reasoning with them.
Others dragged out needlessly difficult psychology terms and tried to explain the rumors away with theory.
All of them said the very same thing.
"Curses don't exist.
Accidents and crimes happen by pure coincidence!"
...Is that really so?
Do coincidences really happen that easily?
{a}...{p}What do you think?
I think it's because of the curse
There's no such thing as curses

No such thing as curses...
So that's what you think.
I see...
I can't blame you. You're still only a first-year.
But you'll only be able to think that way for now.
Because the board's curse is real...
Something happened when I was a first-year.
That was two years ago.
There may well be people who know about it, don't you think?{p}

Back then, there was a school nurse named Eriko Akiyama.
She was still young and pretty, and it seems she often listened to the girls' worries and gave them advice.
Among the problems brought to her was the curse of the Board of Death.
The one who came to her about it was a schoolgirl.
"Ms. Akiyama, do you know about the Board of Death?
It's the bulletin board with all those ominous rumors about it..."
One day...{p}

As punishment for dozing off in class, she got stuck cleaning the bulletin board.
Everyone was so afraid of the curse that they hated even touching it, so the board was completely covered in dust.
Old notices and new ones were plastered all over it, and to clean it she had to tear every one of them down.
The girl let out a sigh and began taking the notices down.
It wasn't that she didn't know the rumors, but being scolded by her teacher scared her even more than the board's curse.
Partway through the job, her eyes were riveted to one sheet of paper.
On that paper,{p}

'It's not fair'
...was all it said, in red letters.
It bothered her a little at the time, but she tried not to think about it and hurried through the cleaning, apparently.
Of course, she took that paper down and threw it away.{p}
For the next two or three days, nothing in particular happened, but...{p}

'You're coming with me too'
was written in bright red ink, they say.
When she saw that message, the board's curse truly terrified her.
And so she went to Ms. Akiyama for advice.
She must have thought Ms. Akiyama, being close to her in age, would surely believe her about the curse.
Ms. Akiyama smiled at the desperate girl's plea and told her this.{p}

"Isn't it just someone's prank?
Girls your age easily lose their emotional balance, and they're very susceptible to suggestion.
Some kids know that and play pranks on you.
I remember being teased like that myself.
At times like this, you mustn't brood over it.
You have to laugh it off, cheerfully!"
So Ms. Akiyama was just like the other teachers after all: someone who didn't believe in ghosts or curses.{p}

Ms. Akiyama didn't believe her, but her smile reassured the girl, who left the nurse's office looking somewhat calmer.
But then...!
From the next day on, she was gone.
...No.
She never went home that day, so to be precise... I should say she vanished after leaving the nurse's office.{p}

Her shoes were still in her shoe locker.
So she had to be somewhere in the school building.
The police came that morning and searched desperately for her.
Right around that time...
a problem had come up among the students, too.{p}

It was that Board of Death.
From around the time the girl went missing, there was an uproar over eerie messages being posted on it.
'One student with a single-digit roll number will die'
'Tomorrow, a student in Class 2-D will be injured'
'I will curse whoever leaves the school building last after school'
One after another, ominous, prophecy-like messages like these kept being posted.
Some people even found the photos from their student handbooks posted there, slashed to ribbons.
Students who couldn't stop shaking with fear...
And students who, on the contrary, crowded in front of the board out of curiosity...{p}

By the time the teachers rushed over, the area in front of the board had fallen into complete panic.
The teachers were desperate to send the confused students back to their classrooms.
But you know, not a single one of the students there would leave the spot.
All of them refused to move, as if their feet had put down roots.
Strangely enough, the teachers couldn't leave that spot either.
Their voices scolding the students grew fainter and fainter...{p}

"Everyone, what are you doing here...?"
When Ms. Akiyama showed up late, the eyes of everyone there were fixed on one spot on the board.
Where they were looking, there was a single sheet of paper.
And on that paper, in bright red letters...{p}

'And you said there was no such thing as curses...'
The moment she saw that paper, Ms. Akiyama's face went pale.
And then, little by little, it flushed red...
"How tasteless, at a time like this☆"
Ms. Akiyama strode up to the board and ripped the paper off in one go.{p}

The thumbtack holding the paper went flying, and from the students crowded around rose small screams of mingled surprise and fear.
"This stupid thing! This stupid thing...☆"
They say Ms. Akiyama, tearing the paper to shreds, looked just like a demon.
Her wide-open eyes were bloodshot, and veins stood out sharply on her forehead...
And when she finally stopped...{p}

"Next it's your turn, Ms. Akiyama..."
Suddenly, from the crowd that had been silent until then, came that murmur.
Whether the voice reached her or not...
Ms. Akiyama, her shoulders heaving with each breath, staggered away.
The next morning...{p}

...Say, {a}.
I was in Class 1-E too.
The classroom at the end of the third-floor hallway.
...Same as you.
Heh heh heh...
Every morning, I went through the front entrance and headed for the stairs at the end of the hallway.
I like empty classrooms.
So I get to school before anyone else, and I hardly ever run into anyone.
But then...
That day, as I was heading for the classroom as usual, a woman was standing by the bulletin board.{p}

It was Ms. Akiyama.
With her back to the board, her arms spread wide...
...What on earth was she doing?
I walked closer, meaning to call out to her.
"Ms. Akiyama......?"
At that moment, I felt something slimy squish under my indoor shoes.{p}

When I looked down, there at my feet was a pool of bright red blood☆
Ms. Akiyama hadn't been standing in front of the board.
She had been pinned up on it.
Nails had been driven into her neck and wrists, and bright red blood was pouring out of them.{p}

Just as someone's murmured prophecy said, this time Ms. Akiyama had fallen victim to the curse.
After the police came and looked into all sorts of things, it was ruled that she had been killed by a deviant who had gotten into the school.
Still, the teachers had stopped denying the students' rumors.
Because the way Ms. Akiyama had acted the day before was just too eerie.
And so they decided to take the Board of Death down, but...{p}

Whenever they tried to start the work, someone always got hurt.
Someone would hit their arm with a hammer, step on a nail, or have something fall on them from above...
It had always had ominous rumors about it, and people had even died.
With accidents like that on top of it all, of course everyone would hate to touch it.
That's why that board is still there even now.
Heh... even now, two years later, the bloodstains and nail holes are still plain to see.
You should take a good look at it on your way home today.{p}

I hear a new message has been posted on it again recently.
As for what sort of message it is...
you'll have to see for yourself.
That's the end of my story.
Shall we move on to the next one...{p}
By the way, {a}...{p}You told a lie a little while ago, didn't you?
Yes
No

Heh heh heh...
That's right. You weren't supposed to know the board existed.
...And yet you knew what it was called.
Since you realize it yourself...
you lied on purpose, didn't you.{p}

I truly, truly hate liars.
Listen.
The board's curse is still going on.
If you keep up that attitude, you'll be cursed someday.
It's simple.
All it takes is posting a paper with your name and roll number on the board on Friday the 13th.
After that, everyone else will spread the rumor for me.{p}

Heh heh heh...
Do be careful, {a}.
...That's the end of my story.
Whose turn is it next, I wonder...?{p}

So you do think it's because of the curse.
I'm glad.
That you believe my story...
I know, let's all go and see it now.
It isn't that late yet, and you'd feel braver with everyone together, wouldn't you?{p}Come now...
Let's go
I don't want to go

Good.
I thought you'd say that.{p}

Oh yes, {a}.
This is for your article, isn't it?
Don't you need to bring your camera?
Here, hold it tight.
Heh heh...
Is there film in it?
I see...
Then we're all set.
Well then, shall we go?{p}

...Here we are.
You pass through here every day, don't you?
The bulletin board is, look, on that wall.{p}Is it too dim for you to make it out...?
Yes
No

That is the Board of Death.
It's old, but it's big, isn't it?{p}Shall we go a little closer...?
Go closer
This is close enough
I want to go back to the club room
There, from this close you can make out every little detail, can't you?

What a shame.
There's nothing posted on it...
I'm sorry.
I got your hopes up, didn't I?

But take a good look at this board...
See, right here.

"She's right..."
Sure enough, there are the words
'The Graduating Class'
...carved there.
Why would a graduation gift have ended up cursed...?
Huh?
Something seems to be carved up near the top, too.
What could it be...?
Let's see...{p}

"Between the students......"
No good, the next characters are too scratched up to read.
But the ones after them seem fine.
"To deep......en the... between the students...?
Oh, I see...{p}

'To deepen the ... between students. The Graduating Class'
...That's what it says.
These graduates must have given us this board with the wish... that we would have a happy school life.
And yet, if they knew it was called 'the Board of Death,' how sad they would be...{p}

"{a}, shall we head back soon?
It's getting cold."
Iwashita and the other five all look somehow uneasy.
I suppose so...
I've confirmed it's a graduation memento, so all that's left is...
"Then I'll just take one last photo."{p}

With that, I raised my camera.
But then...
"Huh...?"
What's wrong?
The shutter won't release.
There's film in it, and the flash is...
Why...★{p}

"Is something wrong?"
"Yes, the shutter won't release.
There shouldn't be anything wrong with it, though..."
"Why don't you try one more time?"
"Okay..."{p}
There was a tremendous crackling snap, and for an instant everything before my eyes went white.{p}

My vision went right back to normal, but my whole body was numb.
"{a}...!"
"You okay★"
Everyone rushed over in surprise.
"That was something, huh?"
"Yeah, it flashed for a second."
"It seems to have been static electricity.
Still, I've never seen it flash that violently before."
Apparently, the instant I pressed the shutter, a current ran right through my body...{p}

"Let's go back, quickly. It's dangerous to stay here any longer."
Held up by the others, my body still numb, I somehow made it back to the club room.{p}

Little by little, the feeling came back to my arms and legs...
"I'm sorry. I never imagined something like this would happen..."
Iwashita said it with her head still bowed.
"No, really. I'm fine.
Please don't worry so much."{p}
"Really...?"{p}
Sure, it hurt a little, but that was nothing to me.{p}

It was the word 'rift.'
And it wasn't carved in properly like the rest. Someone had gouged it in afterward, like graffiti.
To deepen the 'rift' between students...
That word had to be the reason the board was cursed.
And I did feel the shutter go off that time, too...{p}

Now the first of the seven wonders is in the bag.
"Iwashita, thank you for such a lovely... I mean,
for such a scary story.
Well then, shall we move on to the next one...?"{p}

No.
Even if you say you don't want to go, I'm taking you no matter what.{p}
Then let's get a little closer.{p}

Is that so?
Don't say that. Come on...
Let's go forward, just a little more.
That's it...
One step, two steps...
A little more...
It's all right. I'm right here beside you.{p}

My, my...
Are you scared already?
Heh heh heh...
You're quite the scaredy-cat, aren't you, {a}?
...Well.
I suppose we should head back soon.
Something heavy and oppressive is hanging in the air...
It looks like we'd better finish this quickly.
Heh heh. {a}.
Before we go back, you have to take a proper picture...
That's no good from so far away.
Step up closer...
See? There are words carved into the frame, aren't there?

Oh, why would you tell such a lie?
The Class 1-E classroom should be at the end of the hallway on the third floor of the new school building.
I went and checked it myself at lunch today.
Listen, {a}.
I really hate liars.
Answer me honestly.
Your classroom is on the third floor of the new school building.
At the end of the long hallway.
That's correct, isn't it?
Now, nod.{p}

...Yes, that's it. Good.
Heh heh heh...
Then I'll ask you one more thing.
It goes without saying, but you always use the stairs, don't you?{p}

Oh, you know it?
Then this will go quickly.
The story I'm about to tell is about that bulletin board.
That board was a gift the students here left to commemorate their graduation.
They say the new school building hadn't even been built back then, so it must have been decades ago.{p}

Back then, it hung on the first floor of the old school building, they say.
It was meant to deepen the friendship between students, and anyone could use it freely, for anything from club recruitment posters to messages for friends.
The board was covered with notices.
At every break, crowds of students would gather in front of it, and it was always lively, so they say.
I'm sure they passed all kinds of messages to each other.
When the new school building went up, it was moved to where it is now, especially so the students could use it easily.{p}

And yet now, all that's on it is rusty thumbtacks and scraps of paper gone brown, gathering dust...
No one even gives it a glance.
And no wonder.
That board carries a terrible curse.{p}

Oh?
Why, {a}, you're laughing.
Did I say something funny?
Or is it that you can't believe my story?
Either way, I can only take it that you're making fun of me.
Until you apologize, I'm not saying another word.
.................................................................................

What should I do?
I never meant to laugh...
Iwashita is seriously angry.{p}Maybe I should apologize?
Apologize
Don't apologize
Make an excuse: "I wasn't laughing"

I'd better apologize.
It's because I wasn't considerate enough that Iwashita got upset.
Besides, she's my senior.
"I'm truly sorry.
Please forgive me..."{p}

"Heh heh... It's all right.
I'm glad you apologized so honestly.
I adore honest girls.
Oh, I don't mean anything strange by that.
Don't get the wrong idea.
Well then, shall we get back to the story...?"{p}

Where was I?
Oh yes, the board carries a terrible curse.
...That's as far as I got, wasn't it?
Heh heh heh...{p}

That board really is cursed.
Tell me, {a}.
Do you know what that board is called?
It's called 'the Board of Death.'
A loathsome name, isn't it?
But you know...
There's a good reason it's called that.
...The whole curse began with a petty prank.
This was back when the new school building had only just been built.
One day, a single test paper was posted on the board.
A math test, was it?{p}
Well, {a}?{p}Are you good at math?
I'm good at it
I'm bad at it
Neither

Did I ask something unpleasant?
I'm sorry, I didn't know.{p}

But I see...
So you're bad at math.
Heh heh heh...
The test that was posted back then was full of mistakes, too, with an awful score, they say.
The name written on it was...
Heh heh... don't worry.
It wasn't {b} {a}... or anything like that.
The owner of that test paper was named Akiko Eto.{p}

She was plain and quiet, and she didn't stand out much in class.
As for why Eto's test had been posted on the board...
...I think I said this a moment ago, but...
...it was probably just a little prank.
Back then, lots of high school students were still innocent.
I doubt there was much bullying at all.
But you know...{p}

Ashamed, sad, humiliated......
If it were me, I could never bear it.
I'd catch the culprit and get my revenge, no matter what!
...Oh, I'm sorry.
We were talking about Eto, weren't we?{p}

She tore the test off the board and ran straight out.
After that, she never showed her face at school again, they say.{p}

It seems she shut herself up at home the whole time.
And when a week had gone by...{p}

Eto's body was found beside the flower bed in the schoolyard, blood streaming from her head.
She had jumped from the roof.
Leaving one last message on that board... you see.
A suicide note...?
I wonder if you could call it that.{p}

On the back of that test paper of hers,
'It's not fair...'
was written in bright red letters, they say.
There was even a rumor it was written in blood.
It was cleared away at once, so the truth remains a mystery...
But you know...{p}

From then on, eerie messages began to be posted on the board.
'It's not fair...'
'Why is this happening only to me?'
'It's so unfair...'
Every one of them in the same red letters as Eto's suicide note, they say.
It might be someone's prank...
But strangely enough, on any day one of those messages is posted, someone always dies.
And of course, it still goes on to this day.{p}

You be careful too, {a}.
So you don't become one of them...
Heh heh...{p}Well, there is just one way to keep from being killed by the board's curse. Do you want to know?
I want to know
I don't want to know
Then I'll tell you.{p}

If you post that perfect math test on that board, they say her name rises up in bright red letters where the name should be.
And then, from out of nowhere,
"Thank you..."
you hear a girl's voice say.
Only a person who hears that voice can be sure of throwing off the board's curse.{p}

Heh heh heh...
It's thanks to this method that I'm still alive.
{a}, you'd better try it soon too.
There's no point if you die before you score a hundred.
Though I suppose it's a hard method for someone who isn't good at math.
Well, living in fear of the curse might be thrilling and fun, too.
After all, you write better articles when you've felt the fear yourself.
Heh heh...
That's the end of my story.
I'm looking forward to the next one.{p}

Heh heh...
Are you sure you should be saying that?
Don't you think losing your life to a curse would be ridiculous...?
Whether you try the method or not is up to you...
You can decide after you've heard it, can't you?
...I'll tell you.

Actually, I...
went to look at the board before I came here.
Heh heh, I always make a point of looking whenever I pass by it.
Hoping something might be posted there...
I've never found anything yet.
Sadly, I didn't see anything like that today either.
Heh heh heh...
Be careful, {a}.
The people who died from Eto's curse were all good at math.
She must envy people who are good at math.
The next time a message is posted, the one who loses their life might be you.
Scared...?
Then good.
Today is the seven wonders meeting, isn't it?
You write better articles when you've felt the fear yourself.
Heh heh...
That's the end of my story.
I'm looking forward to the next one.{p}

I'm not apologizing.
I wasn't laughing at all.
This is a ridiculous accusation!
You're just enjoying picking on me because I'm new, aren't you?
What a nasty person...
Come to think of it, I heard someone gossiping about it before.
That there's a seriously terrifying senior in Class 3-A...
A senior who always keeps a box cutter hidden in a pocket, and who, when irritated, always slides the blade in and out to calm down...{p}

Click... click...
It was only a rumor, so the name wasn't clear, but I think it was I-senpai......

Click-click-click...
What is this sound I keep hearing?
......Oh!
Could I-senpai be......★
Wh-what should I do?{p}M-maybe I should apologize......
Apologize
Don't apologize

No, I still don't want to apologize!
I can't lie to my own heart.
I really wasn't laughing.
Why should I have to apologize?
And then...{p}

"Heh heh heh...
It seems you have no intention of apologizing, {a}, no matter what.
Well, it can't be helped.
That's the end of my story.
Go on to the next one..."
Iwashita twisted her mouth into an eerie smile.
And then, that sound again...

Anyway, I'll just apologize.
"I'm sorry.
It was my fault.
Please forgive me..."
"Oh, so you're apologizing?
Then you were laughing at me after all.
What a nasty girl!

Apologizing would make it look like I did something wrong, and I hate that.
But leaving things awkward by not apologizing is a little...
In that case, I have to make it clear that I wasn't laughing.
"Um... Iwashita."
"Oh?
Have you decided to apologize?"
"No, it's not that.
I just wanted to clear up a misunderstanding...
I absolutely was not laughing."
"...I see."
Huh?
That's all?{p}It looks like she has no intention of going on with the story until I apologize.
Apologize
Don't apologize

You're good at it?
I see...
To say it so flatly, you must be quite confident.
But that's a little surprising.
That you're good at math...
You really can't judge people by appearances.{p}

...Oh, I'm sorry.
I'm not putting you down.
I'm honestly impressed, that's all.
But I see...
So you're good at math.
Heh heh heh...
The test that was posted back then was full of mistakes, with an awful score, they say.
The name written on it was Akiko Eto.{p}

Heh heh heh...
So you're neither good nor bad at it.
Meaning your scores go up and down from test to test?
I see...
Lots of people are like that.
If only it had been one of the times with a good score...
The test that was posted back then was full of mistakes, with an awful score, they say.
The name written on it was...
Heh heh... don't worry.
It wasn't {b} {a}... or anything like that.
The owner of that test paper was named Akiko Eto.
